items.proposal: MEASURED by the orchestrator's gate script over the two landed packets (the gate evaluation, pinned); the content of each lane's finding is REPORTED by that lane. Check both on the pinned bytes before you rule. E11 ordered one exact replacement in row W4-004, boundary_evidence_refs entry 1. It is installed; the entry now reads, in full: "oshb:Dan.7.14 [WARRANT-onset:far] everlasting_dominion_aram at words 12 to 14 of 21 in the closing verse of the vision report; PE after this verse (OSHB mark layer; single witness; informs, never decides)". Lane TB challenges that record (W10#2), grade low, and asks a row change. Its claim, verbatim: "The entry is right that oshb Dan.7.14 has 21 words, that the inventory lists everlasting_dominion_aram at Dan.7.14, and that PE follows the verse. It is one word wide on where the device stands: the inventory pattern matches words 13 to 14, and word 12 is the possessed noun of the dominion clause, which the pattern does not match. Words 12 to 14 are the clause that carries the device, not the device." Its evidence, verbatim: ["python -B work\\s3.py (own script, in OUT\\work; reads the pinned inputs only) -> Dan.7.14 split on whitespace: 21 words (no maqqef, paseq or other non-letter, non-mark character in the verse line)", "python -B work\\s3.py (own script, in OUT\\work; reads the pinned inputs only) -> inventory pattern \"שלטן\\\\s+עלם\" searched over the mark-stripped words of Dan.7.14: one match, words 13 to 14, 'שלטן עלם'; words 12 to 14 are שלטנה שלטן עלם (pointed: שָׁלְטָנֵ֞הּ שָׁלְטָ֤ן עָלַם֙); word 12 has medial nun and a suffix and is outside the match", "SP\\Dan\\dan_device_inventory.json formulae.everlasting_dominion_aram: gloss \"'an everlasting dominion' (Aramaic)\", count 2, verses_mt [Dan.4.31, Dan.7.14]; the entry holds verses and a pattern, and no word positions", "SP\\Dan\\pmarks_Dan.json marks['Dan.7.14'] = ['PE'], marks['Dan.7.13'] and marks['Dan.7.15'] absent; witness 'WLC (OSHB) - single witness; disclose on every citation'", "SP\\Dan\\fixup\\draft_rows_fixup9_applied.jsonl: W4-003 span Dan.7.13-Dan.7.14, W4-004 span Dan.7.15-Dan.7.18; SP\\Dan\\Dan_web_clean.txt 7:15 '[v] 15 “As for me, Daniel, my spirit was grieved within my body, and the visions of my head troubled me.': Dan.7.14 is the last verse before the seer's reaction, so 'the closing verse of the vision report' is a reading the bytes do not refute (the E11 order gives this list field no tier word)", "SP\\Dan\\fixup\\draft_rows_fixup9_applied.jsonl row W4-004 boundary_rationale, same row: 'the dominion clause at words 12 to 14 of its 21, where everlasting_dominion_aram is listed', and words 18 to 21 end the verse; SP\\Dan\\review\\dan_controlling_agent_rulings_E11.v1.json RR8-LOW-EXTRAS evidence: 'words 12 to 14 are the dominion clause'. Both name the clause at 12 to 14; the ordered after text attaches the device name to that range", "E11 RR8-LOW-EXTRAS orders[0].exact_spans: entry_index 1, before 'everlasting_dominion_aram closes the vision report', after 'everlasting_dominion_aram at words 12 to 14 of 21 in the closing verse of the vision report' (equal to the extract's record); applied exactly: after count 1, before count 0"] Its decision, verbatim: "Correction owed, low: say that the dominion clause stands at words 12 to 14 of 21 and the device at words 13 to 14, for example 'everlasting_dominion_aram at words 13 to 14 of 21, inside the dominion clause at words 12 to 14, in the closing verse of the vision report'. The fault lies in the after text E11 ordered, not in how the author applied it. No boundary argument rests on the one word: the range given contains the device words, and the count, the listing and the mark are true." Its answer to the ordered check that the entry agrees with the verse and the inventory is no; the bytes it read, verbatim: "entry: 'oshb:Dan.7.14 [WARRANT-onset:far] everlasting_dominion_aram at words 12 to 14 of 21 in the closing verse of the vision report; PE after this verse (OSHB mark layer; single witness; informs, never decides)' | SP\\Dan\\Dan_oshb.txt Dan.7.14 has 21 words by script: 1:ולה 2:יהיב 3:שלטן 4:ויקר 5:ומלכו 6:וכל 7:עממיא 8:אמיא 9:ולשניא 10:לה 11:יפלחון 12:שלטנה 13:שלטן 14:עלם 15:די 16:לא 17:יעדה 18:ומלכותה 19:די 20:לא 21:תתחבל | SP\\Dan\\dan_device_inventory.json everlasting_dominion_aram pattern \"שלטן\\\\s+עלם\", verses_mt [\"Dan.4.31\", \"Dan.7.14\"] | the device words stand at words 13 to 14 (one match); word 12 is outside the pattern. Agrees on the count of 21, on the listing at Dan.7.14 and on the PE after the verse; does not agree on the first word of the device's place (12 written, 13 in the bytes). The answer is true if 'at words 12 to 14' is read as the clause that carries the device." Lane OS supports the same record and answers the same check yes; the bytes it read, verbatim: "Entry: 'oshb:Dan.7.14 [WARRANT-onset:far] everlasting_dominion_aram at words 12 to 14 of 21 in the closing verse of the vision report; PE after this verse (OSHB mark layer; single witness; informs, never decides)' Dan_oshb.txt Dan.7.14 has 21 words, all in Hebrew square script (the Aramaic of the verse; no word in any other script; no maqqef in the file's line): 1 וְלֵ֨הּ 2 יְהִ֤יב 3 שָׁלְטָן֙ 4 וִיקָ֣ר 5 וּמַלְכ֔וּ 6 וְכֹ֣ל 7 עַֽמְמַיָּ֗א 8 אֻמַיָּ֛א 9 וְלִשָּׁנַיָּ֖א 10 לֵ֣הּ 11 יִפְלְח֑וּן 12 שָׁלְטָנֵ֞הּ 13 שָׁלְטָ֤ן 14 עָלַם֙ 15 דִּֽי 16 לָ֣א 17 יֶעְדֵּ֔ה 18 וּמַלְכוּתֵ֖הּ 19 דִּי 20 לָ֥א 21 תִתְחַבַּֽל. The device words stand at 12 to 14: שָׁלְטָנֵ֞הּ שָׁלְטָ֤ן עָלַם֙; the inventory pattern שלטן\\s+עלם matches words 13 to 14, and word 12 is the head noun of the same clause. Words 15 to 17 and 18 to 21 follow, so the device does not close the verse; the verse does close the vision report (W4-003 span Dan.7.13-Dan.7.14, PE after Dan.7.14 in pmarks_Dan.json). Inventory entry named: formulae.everlasting_dominion_aram {\"gloss\": \"'an everlasting dominion' (Aramaic)\", \"language\": \"Aramaic\", \"pattern\": \"שלטן\\\\s+עלם\", \"count\": 2, \"verses_mt\": [\"Dan.4.31\", \"Dan.7.14\"], \"cross_language_hits\": [], \"web_for_zone_refs\": {\"Dan.4.31\": \"web:Dan.4.34\"}} : it lists Dan.7.14." Both lanes report the same measurement and differ only in how they read the phrase. The after text was worded by ruling E11 and applied exactly as ordered; neither lane faults the author. Proposal by the orchestrator: run a script of your own on oshb Dan.7.14 and on the inventory pattern of the device the entry names, then choose one of three. (a) The entry states a place the bytes do not bear and must be corrected before the boss reads it: order one exact span under a new part W11, stated against the installed FIXUP-9 rows, and set the gate to fixup10_ordered. Before you order it, test every number and every factual word of your after text by script on the pinned bytes, and put the command and its output in the ruling's evidence; the after text E11 ordered was not so tested, and that is how this return arose. (b) The entry is true as a statement of the clause that carries the device and imprecise as a statement of the device's own extent, no boundary argument rests on the one word, and it is of a class that may wait: route it to fable_end_review by row, field and entry, and set the gate to routed_to_end_review. (c) The finding does not hold on the bytes: close it with the reason and set the gate to closed_no_defect. Regrade nothing by assertion: give the scale words you rely on.
